newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Five massacred in Karachi violence.
newsitem.headline: Five massacred in Karachi violence.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen killed five young men on Wednesday in the industrial port city of Karachi in southern Pakistan, police said.
The police said the men were driven at gunpoint to the Ghaziabad area of Orangi Extension in District West and then shot dead in a street.
The killers fled in the vehicle which had been earlier stolen from another part of the city, police said.
The five bodies were taken to the government's Abbasi Shaheed Hospital at Paposhnager for identification and post mortem, police said. "Their political affiliation is not available."
No group claimed responsibility for the killings.
Violence has surged in Karachi in recent weeks in renewed feuding between militants of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and its MQM-Haqiqi splinter faction.
At least 125 people have died in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi this year, compared to about 500 last year and more than 2,000 in 1995.
The MQM was brought into a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, after national and provincial elections in February.
